case_name: Hey Listen Mandyhan, L.L.C. v. Trody

issues.label: Jurisdiction under R.C. 1923
issues.why: The court must confirm it has subject-matter and territorial jurisdiction to hear a forcible entry and detainer action for this parcel.

issues.label: Proper plaintiff standing
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mandyhan, as titled owner (or proper agent), is the real party in interest entitled to seek possession.

issues.label: Proper defendant/occupant status
issues.why: The court must determine Trody’s legal status (tenant, vendee, holdover, or purchaser-in-possession) because it controls remedies and process.

issues.label: Existence of landlord-tenant relation
issues.why: FED requires a present right to possession usually arising from a landlord-tenant relationship unless another basis for possession is shown.

issues.label: Which agreement(s) govern
issues.why: The court must decide whether the lease alone controls or whether the lease and purchase agreement must be read together as one transaction.

issues.label: Integration clause effect
issues.why: The lease’s integration clause raises whether extrinsic contemporaneous agreements can modify or be considered with the lease.

issues.label: Parol evidence admissibility
issues.why: If the lease is integrated/unambiguous, the court must determine whether testimony about a purchase arrangement is admissible to vary its terms.

issues.label: Contract ambiguity determination
issues.why: The court must decide whether the documents are ambiguous and, if so, interpret them by intent and surrounding circumstances.

issues.label: Lease vs option vs sale
issues.why: The court must classify the transaction as a true lease, a lease-with-option, an executory purchase, or a disguised financing contract.

issues.label: Land installment contract classification
issues.why: The court must decide whether the combined documents constitute a land installment contract under R.C. 5313.01-.02.

issues.label: Residential property predicate
issues.why: R.C. 5313 applies only if the real property is “improved by virtue of a dwelling having been erected,” requiring a correct legal reading of that definition.

issues.label: Meaning of “dwelling erected”
issues.why: The court must determine whether conversion of an existing structure into living space can satisfy the statutory dwelling predicate or whether new construction is required.

issues.label: What qualifies as a dwelling
issues.why: The court must decide whether the renovated garage/apartment is a “dwelling” under the applicable statutory or common-law meaning.

issues.label: Effect of zoning on dwelling status
issues.why: The court must consider whether commercial zoning or nonconforming residential use affects whether a structure counts as a dwelling for R.C. 5313 purposes.

issues.label: Illegality/nonconforming use defenses
issues.why: If residential occupancy violates zoning/building codes, the court must decide what effect that has on enforceability and available remedies.

issues.label: Substantial compliance with R.C. 5313.02
issues.why: If the writings do not strictly meet statutory elements, the court must decide whether substantial compliance can create an enforceable land installment contract.

issues.label: Mandatory R.C. 5313.02 terms
issues.why: The court must evaluate which statutory disclosures/terms are required and whether their absence voids, voids in part, or alters remedies.

issues.label: Down payment characterization
issues.why: The $3,000 “down payment” versus “security deposit” must be characterized because it affects whether the deal is purchase financing or a lease.

issues.label: Monthly payment characterization
issues.why: The court must determine whether the $459.10 (or $570/$574) payments are rent, purchase installments, or mixed payments.

issues.label: Taxes/insurance allocation
issues.why: The court must decide whether shifting taxes/assessments/insurance to Trody indicates ownership-like obligations supporting an installment contract.

issues.label: Default amount and timing
issues.why: The court must determine precisely when default occurred (March/April/May) and the amount due to assess notice sufficiency and right to possession.

issues.label: Tender after notice effect
issues.why: The court must decide whether Trody’s attempted tender after notice cured default, and whether Mandyhan’s refusal preserves or waives rights.

issues.label: Waiver by accepting late payments
issues.why: Payment history through March 2025 may show waiver of strict compliance or a course of dealing affecting default and termination.

issues.label: Lease termination requirements
issues.why: If a lease governs, the court must determine what termination/default provisions apply and whether they were followed.

issues.label: Option termination requirements
issues.why: If the purchase agreement is an option, the court must decide whether default under the lease extinguishes the option and under what terms.

issues.label: R.C. 5313.06 ten-day notice
issues.why: If this is a land installment contract, the vendor must give a ten-day notice to cure before forfeiture, affecting whether the action is premature.

issues.label: Sufficiency of May 2 notice
issues.why: Even under FED, the court must determine whether the three-day notice complied with statutory content, service, and timing requirements.

issues.label: Notice service and proof
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether posting by Hill constituted proper service and whether proof of service is adequate.

issues.label: Notice cure opportunity required
issues.why: The court must decide whether any cure opportunity beyond three days was legally required by statute or contract given the transaction’s characterization.

issues.label: R.C. 5313.07 foreclosure threshold
issues.why: If R.C. 5313 applies and Trody paid ≥20% of purchase price, the court must decide whether foreclosure (not eviction) is the exclusive remedy.

issues.label: 20% calculation methodology
issues.why: The court must decide how to calculate the percentage paid—what counts as “paid” toward purchase price versus interest, taxes, insurance, or rent.

issues.label: Ledger admissibility and weight
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mandyhan’s ledger is admissible, reliable, and sufficient to prove payment history and allocation.

issues.label: Judicial notice requests handling
issues.why: The court must rule whether requested “judicial notice” of calculations/ledger matters is proper under Evidence Rule 201 and whether failure to rule is error.

issues.label: Credibility findings and deference
issues.why: Resolution depends on witness credibility (Marie vs Trody), requiring explicit findings and proper deference on review of a magistrate’s decision.

issues.label: Scope of FED proceeding
issues.why: The court must determine whether the issues raised (contract characterization, title-like claims) exceed FED’s limited scope or can be decided as defenses.

issues.label: Right to possession vs title
issues.why: FED determines possession, not title, so the court must ensure it is not improperly adjudicating ownership while resolving defenses.

issues.label: Effect of simultaneous execution dates
issues.why: The court must determine the legal significance of executing documents “simultaneously” and the effective date discrepancy for contract formation.

issues.label: Authority of signatory (Grabow)
issues.why: The court must confirm Mark Grabow had authority to bind Mandyhan to a purchase/financing arrangement if such agreement is enforced.

issues.label: Agency of Hill posting notice
issues.why: The court must confirm Hill had authority to serve notice on Mandyhan’s behalf and that service complied with statute.

issues.label: Consideration and enforceability
issues.why: The court must ensure both agreements are supported by consideration and are not illusory, especially if treated as an option or installment contract.

issues.label: Remedy selection and exclusivity
issues.why: Depending on characterization, the court must choose the correct remedy (eviction, forfeiture, foreclosure) and ensure statutory exclusivity is honored.

issues.label: Mootness of substantial compliance
issues.why: If the dwelling predicate is satisfied, substantial compliance becomes material; if not, the court must ensure it is truly moot as a legal matter.

issues.label: Statutory interpretation of R.C. 5313.01(B)
issues.why: The court must correctly interpret the statute’s text and legislative purpose to decide whether existing structures can qualify as “dwelling erected.”

issues.label: Equitable defenses/estoppel
issues.why: Trody’s reliance and improvements allegedly approved by Mandyhan may support estoppel or equitable defenses affecting forfeiture/possession.

issues.label: Improvements and reimbursement claims
issues.why: The court must consider whether claims about improvements affect possession rights or require separate proceedings and whether they bar immediate eviction.

issues.label: Material breach determination
issues.why: The court must decide whether nonpayment for April/May (or March/April) is a material breach justifying termination/possession.

issues.label: Acceptance/refusal of partial payments
issues.why: The court must determine whether refusal of arrearage payments was contractually/statutorily permissible and its effect on default and notice.

issues.label: Consistency of rent amount evidence
issues.why: Conflicting rent figures ($459.10 vs $570/$574) require the court to find the actual obligation and whether arrears were proven by a preponderance.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must allocate burdens: plaintiff’s burden to prove right to possession and notice; defendant’s burden on affirmative defenses (e.g., 5313 applicability).

issues.label: Magistrate procedure compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure proper handling of the motion for judgment, evidentiary rulings, and issuance of findings/conclusions under civil rules.

issues.label: Objections review standard
issues.why: The trial court must apply the correct standard when ruling on objections to a magistrate’s decision, including independent review of objected matters.

issues.label: Record adequacy for review
issues.why: The court must ensure the transcript/exhibits support findings and that missing rulings (e.g., judicial notice) do not impair due process.

issues.label: Due process in eviction timing
issues.why: The court must ensure statutory notice and hearing requirements were satisfied so the occupant received adequate process before dispossession.

issues.label: Attorney fees/costs authorization
issues.why: If costs or fees are sought, the court must determine whether statute or contract authorizes them in an FED context.

issues.label: Relief limited to restitution
issues.why: The court must ensure the judgment in FED is limited to restitution of premises and costs, leaving damages/accounting to separate claims if necessary.
